item.description:
v0.3.9: A clearer battery floor for a closed lid
- The Awake setting that ends the closed-lid hold on battery now reads "On battery, stop the closed-lid hold below 15%". It used to read "let the lid go below", which sounded as if the percentage belonged to the lid rather than to the battery. The confirmation shown when you switch on Keep working with the lid closed is reworded the same way.

v0.3.8: GitHub contributions that match your profile
- The Forge tab's GitHub contributions now agree with the count on your github.com profile. They were read from an API that leaves out part of the private work the profile counts, so they read low, by 12 on one day measured. GitHub Enterprise keeps the API figure.

v0.3.7: Codex back on the Overview after a relaunch
- Codex no longer disappears from the Overview after Sissy restarts, as it did after the 0.3.6 update for anyone who had archived a Codex session in the last two days. Archiving a session moves its log out of the folder Sissy reads, and Sissy then threw away everything it had counted from it. - A signed-in Codex or Claude account with nothing spent in the last two days still gets its row, with its plan and its limits, instead of waiting for the next turn to show up.

v0.3.6: accounts named by who owns them, and each one's plan in view
- Accounts are named after their owner or their team: a personal plan takes your name, or your address when claude.ai has no name for it, and a team seat takes the organisation's. Settings › Providers picks the format (Automatic, Email, or Name and organisation), and each account's ⋯ menu there has Rename… for a name of your own. An empty name goes back to the automatic one. - With more than one account for a vendor, each row on the Overview carries its plan as a badge beside the name, so a Max seat and a Team one are told apart at a glance. The rows are grouped under their vendor and spaced to match. - A window that has not started yet says "starts on first use" under its bar instead of leaving the line empty. - Use in CLI moved into the account menu on the provider page, which also marks the account the CLI is signed into. - A Max 20x account reads "Max 20x" again, where it showed plain "Max".

v0.3.5: one label per vendor, resets in view, and a keep-awake that counts from when you ask
- The Overview names a vendor once over all of its accounts. Each account keeps its own bar, and every row says when its window resets, so how long until a full account works again is on the first page. - A degraded vendor status colours the vendor's name only, never the account beside it. - The Sessions tab draws the day's work blocks for a single past day picked on the calendar, not only for today. - Keep awake: a duration picked while the Mac is already held now counts from that moment, where it used to end the hold at once. Switching the lid on, or switching to Always, starts the count again. - With the lid closed on battery, Sissy lets the lid go below a charge you choose in Settings › Awake, 15% by default. - Switching Claude accounts no longer refuses when one of Claude Code's saved sign-ins is an older copy of an account Sissy already holds. The warning from a failed switch clears as soon as the signed-in account changes, and the log names the sign-in that could not be identified. - Pricing knows claude-haiku-5-5 out of the box.

v0.3.4: an account switch Claude Code follows, an honest disk reading, and forge counts that add up
- Switching Claude accounts from Sissy now also points Claude Code's own config file at the new account, so the CLI's requests go to that account's organisation. Sessions already open follow it without a restart. - The Disk tab reads free space the way the system does when a write needs it. What macOS could reclaim on its own is shown apart as "macOS can free", explained on hover, and never counted as free. - The Disk tab no longer offers to clear caches: the tools that fill them refill them on their next run. - GitHub merges and issues for a picked span count only what falls inside it, where they could count every merge the account ever made. - Forge counters count the day from your local midnight, where a day's contributions could stay hidden until midnight UTC. - Every log line is dated, and the log records Claude account changes and resets that were expected and did not appear.

v0.3.3: Claude Code resets, a calendar for the period, and a Mac that keeps working with its lid closed
- Claude Code's provider page shows the usage-limit resets Anthropic gave the account, with a button that spends one after asking. It names the windows the reset clears and when it lapses, and a press only ever spends for the account the page showed it under. - The period control opens a calendar: pick a day or drag across a run of days, and the headline, the projects and the forge counters all follow it. A picked period goes back to Today after 24 hours. - Keep-awake can hold the Mac working with its lid closed. It is off by default, asks before it changes anything, and is cleared at the next launch if Sissy did not get to clear it itself. - Keep-awake has its own Settings tab, where Always can hold for a set time or with no limit, and the cup's menu switches the screen half of the hold and the lid. - The cup in the menu bar is drawn as one glyph sized to the gear beside it, and only its steam says a hold is on.

v0.3.2: GitHub Actions minutes on the Forge tab
- The Forge tab shows how much of each GitHub owner's monthly Actions allowance is gone, the account and every organisation whose bill the token can read, with a gauge that resets on the 1st and a line naming the repository and runner that spent the most. It has its own switch, and reading the account's own bill needs the `user` scope on the token. - Only private repositories count against the allowance, the way GitHub bills it; larger runners stay out of it. - The Codex reset button is offered whenever a reset is held, including while the session limit sits at 100%.

v0.3.1: Steadier readings, lighter on the Mac
- The panel header keeps one wording instead of flipping between a long and a short form, and stays on one line beside its controls. - A keep-awake request that gets no answer now expires on its own. - The refresh buttons' tooltips say what the button does. - A Codex limit whose reset the CLI leaves empty is kept rather than dropped. - When a vendor answers "too many requests", Sissy waits as long as it was told before asking again. - Sissy saves its usage state before the Mac sleeps and rewrites it less often while it runs. - Reading the CLIs' logs and drawing the panel costs less CPU, and an export no longer holds up the panel. - Rates for gpt-6.1-sol. - Fixes to limits polling, account linking and frame ordering.

v0.3.0: A tab for each thing Sissy watches
- The panel moves between modules with a row of tabs: Overview, Sessions, Mac, Disk, Network and Forge. The period (Today, 7 days, 30 days, All) is chosen once, in the header, and every tab reads over it. - Sessions has its own tab, with the running ones folded behind one row. - Disk has its own tab and badge: free space, read and write activity while the tab is open, and the caches taking room. - Clean regenerable caches from the Disk tab: Xcode DerivedData, npm, uv and iOS device support. Each asks before it removes anything, and one is refused while its tool is at work. - A separate row takes only the Xcode builds of projects that no longer exist, such as deleted worktrees, so the projects you still have keep theirs. - A Network tab shows traffic while it is on screen. Network and disk rates are logged every five seconds in the background, so the charts are full when you open them. - Each forge has its own section on the Forge tab, with the latest thing you did there. Switch that line off under Settings > Forge > Latest activity. - Disk and Network have their own switches under Settings > Mac.

v0.2.9: See how the Mac is holding up
- A Mac line on the Overview shows the kernel's memory pressure and the free disk, orange at warn and red at critical. - The Mac has its own page: memory, swap and free disk, load against the cores, uptime, and the three apps holding the most memory outside your agents. - Under pressure, a small orange or red dot appears behind Sissy's neck in the menu bar. The blue eye still means only that the Mac is held awake. - Switch it off under Settings > General > Mac health. It asks for no permission.

v0.2.8: Link a Claude account with Google or email
- Continue with Google on the claude.ai sign-in now works: its popup opens over the page in the same window and hands the sign-in back when it closes. - Signing in with email no longer leaves you on claude.ai's own app inside the window without linking the account. - The window that asks which organisation to link, or says a link failed, is sized to what it says rather than drawn as tall as the screen.

v0.2.7: Spend a Codex reset from Sissy
- The Codex page now shows the resets your account holds and when the next one expires. Once OpenAI would apply one, when a window is nearly used up, a Use… button spends it for the account the page is showing. - Sissy asks before spending, and trying again after an answer that never arrived cannot spend a second reset.

v0.2.6: Update checks you can watch
- Check for Updates in About now checks in place: a spinner, then the answer under the button (up to date, a new version, or a check that could not reach the feed), with no window in the way. A new version turns the button into Update to it, which opens the usual update alert. - The notice about a Claude Code sign-in Sissy does not read is now a short, clearly marked warning, and it no longer appears for a folder you stopped using weeks ago.

v0.2.5: Sissy updates itself
- Sissy checks for new versions on its own and installs one only when you say so. The controls sit at the foot of About: the current version, a Check for Updates button, and a switch for automatic checks. - Updates are signed and notarized, and Sissy verifies each one before installing it. - This is the last version you install by hand: 0.2.4 cannot update itself, so download 0.2.5 once and later versions arrive through Sissy. - About's links stay blue and the sheet ends on the copyright line.
